summary: The privileged account it-admin logged in successfully from 203.0.113.88 after 48 failed attempts within 10 minutes, a pattern consistent with a brute-force or password-spray compromise. The alert has no context on whether the source IP is known or whether the failures were a user mistyping or an automated service, so compromise cannot be confirmed or ruled out yet.

evidence.why: 48 failures in a short window is far beyond normal typos and points to automated guessing or credential stuffing, which is a malicious signal.
The high-velocity burst (about 5 attempts per minute) supports automated attack behavior rather than human error.

A successful login right after the failures suggests the attacker may have guessed the password. A stale-credential service or a locked-out admin retrying could also explain it, so this signal is ambiguous.
This is a privileged account, so a compromise would have a high impact and justifies a fast response.
There is no reputation, geolocation, or allowlist information. If the IP belongs to the corporate VPN or an admin workstation, this could be benign, but that is unverified.

recommended_action.detail: Escalate to L2/IR now. Contact the it-admin owner out of band to confirm whether they made these logins. Check IAM and auth logs for post-login activity from 203.0.113.88 (new sessions, privilege changes, MFA changes, new accounts), and check the IP's reputation and whether it is a known corporate or VPN address. If the owner cannot confirm, reset the credentials, revoke active sessions, and block the IP.
